# Signing out with open windows logs an insertNodeBatch error per window

## Context

Emmy's independent capture for #21087's Round 2 logged two console errors, and they reproduce at `c4e6556490`: at 1280×800, sign in, open Mail and Calendar, then sign out.

```
insertNodeBatch: Parent not found {parentId: neo-component-7, index: 4}
insertNodeBatch: Parent not found {parentId: neo-component-9, index: 4}
```

`neo-component-7` and `neo-component-9` are the two windows' `WebDesktop.view.AppView`s. With one window open there is one error, and with none there is none.

## The Problem

Signing out paints the console red, once for each open window. Nothing visible breaks, since the windows are leaving anyway. But the demo is the engine's featured example for 14.0, and an error on its most basic action invites a stranger to distrust everything after it. A console listener in a test would also fail on it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `WebDesktop.view.ViewportController#onSignOutButtonClick` calls `hideAllWindows()` and then `setState({account: null, …})` synchronously. `hideAllWindows()` hides each window inside `promise.then()`, so every hide runs one microtask after the state change.
- The state change reaches each window's `AppView` through its `account` binding. `afterSetAccount` calls `renderCard()`, which rebuilds the card and calls `update()`. The window is still mounted then, so the update goes out to the VDOM worker.
- `Neo.dialog.Base#hide(false)` unmounts a body-level window through `component.Base#unmount()`. That sends `removeNode` straight to the main thread, which applies it before the AppView's update returns. The insert batch then finds no parent.
- In the other order, the engine already handles this: `unmount()` sets `mounted = false`, `container.Base#afterSetMounted` cascades it to the items (#19973), and an update on an unmounted component waits for its next mount (`VdomLifecycle#updateVdom`).
- Design authority: n/a. The defect excuse is the fenced console error above.

## The Fix

- `onSignOutButtonClick` awaits `hideAllWindows()` before it changes the state, and `hideAllWindows()` returns the promise of all hides. `pendingSignIn` is still cleared synchronously, so a sign-in reading its arrangement is cancelled at the click, as before.
- A unit arm in `ViewportController.spec.mjs` proves the order: every window is hidden before the state changes.
- No e2e arm. A console-listening e2e spec stayed green on the pre-fix head under the e2e harness, even after both windows finished opening, so it cannot catch this race and would only look like coverage. The unit arm carries the order, and a browser witness carries the symptom.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 signing out with two windows open logs no console error. Browser witness: two errors at the pre-fix head, none at the fix.
- [ ] AC-2 the windows are hidden before the account changes (unit).
- [ ] AC-3 a sign-out still cancels a sign-in that is reading its arrangement (the existing arm stays green).

## Out of Scope

- The engine's handling of an update that is already in flight when an ancestor unmounts. The app fix removes the ordering; a guard in the delta pipeline would be a separate engine question.
- `AppView`'s full-card rebuild in `renderCard()`.

## Avoided Traps

- Skipping `renderCard()` for a `null` account. That hides this one trigger, not the ordering: any later state a window's content binds would race the same way.

## Related

- #21061 (parent epic), #21064 / #21073 (the windows, where this ordering began), #21087 (the stack this fix sits on), #19973 (the mounted cascade)
